To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a deep feedforward neural network architecture for semantic scene labeling that is orders of magnitude faster and outperforms previous methods on the Stanford Background and SIFT Flow dataset.

we propose a novel recursive neural net architecture, rCPN, for semantic scene labeling that is orders of magnitude faster (0.07 sec) than existing methods and that it achieves the state-of-the-art performance (79% accuracy) on Stanford background dataset and 70% accuracy on the SIFT Flow dataset, both using only RGB pixel values.
We present a new deep feed-forward network for semantic labeling.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of semantic scene labeling.
the development of deep neural networks for semantic scene labeling and the development of a new architecture for context propagation.
developing a deep neural network architecture that is able to propagate information from every location to every other location and that is computationally efficient.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we present an efficient, fast and accurate method for semantic scene labeling.
the proposed approach outperforms previous state-of-the-art approaches on the Stanford Background dataset by a large margin.
the proposed method is the first that combines the advantages of a deep feed-forward network architecture and recursive context propagation in a unified framework.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel deep feed-forward neural architecture that is orders of magnitude faster and achieves state-of-the-art results on the Stanford background dataset.

we propose a novel neural network architecture for semantic segmentation of scenes that outperforms previous methods, is orders of magnitude faster, and is more robust to the choice of the number of super-pixels.
we have shown that it is possible to build a fast, accurate and end-to-end trainable semantic segmentation network that can be trained using a single GPU.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed rCPN architecture can be applied to any other task that requires context propagation.

the proposed method can be trained end-to-end from raw RGB pixel intensities to pixel-wise labels, without any pre-segmentation of the image, which is a very important step towards a complete scene understanding system.
a feed-forward neural network can outperform recurrent networks for semantic scene labeling.
